items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: So my music teacher was Eugenia K. Reynaud, as I previously stated

ctx.x: You know, this comes to my mind about Ma Rainey, of course the very famous old blues singer, came to Lake Charles from Texas, and with her little five piece band. She needed a pianist. Her pianist had quit in Beaumont, Texas, and so they played this little theater in Lake Charles called the Palace Theater, and whoever the leader was, I don't even remember the musicians now, wouldn't remember any of their names, but they wanted -- they needed a piano player, they had to have a piano player for her. And so they…

said, "Well, I wonder do you think we could get her to help us out?" Because there really wasn't anybody else around that time who read too well, you know. And so he says, "Well, I'll ask her." So then he came down to my home, and we lived about a block and a half from this Palace Theater, on Boulevard, and so he came down and he asked my mother if they would let me -- if she would let me play, and she says, "Well, you'll have to ask her music teacher if she thinks she can play well enough." So my music teacher…
What was the school, what was the name
